experiment: ELUDe-inspired contribution-mode split frozen causal gate
motivation: Test whether distinct input-contribution modes inside one V396 feature can be separated into low-k readable responses without labels, parameter growth, or exposed-dimension growth before developing a jointly trainable module.

source.paper: Interpretability Without Tradeoffs: Disentangling Polysemanticity At Equal Predictive Performance

training_data.policy: read-only; metadata manifest must be identical before and after fitting
training_data.activation_source: same flat L22 activation cache used by existing baselines

representation.definition: For each selected parent, partition its encoder weight additively from two contribution-mode representatives. Route the original nonnegative V396 response between the two subresponses using normalized positive split preactivations. Fold one low-usage recipient response into the first slot so every parent-recipient pair preserves total activation mass and the total exposed dimension remains 65536.
representation.parent_selection: largest balanced two-mode contribution separation on unlabeled OWT tokens
representation.recipient_selection: lowest unlabeled OWT mean V396 activation, disjoint from parents

wrong_control.definition: Apply a deterministic nonzero circular permutation to each learned input-coordinate allocation vector before multiplying by the same parent encoder row. This preserves each allocation multiset and additive parent decomposition while breaking alignment to the contribution modes.

gate.pass_action: Develop one exact-parameter, exact-exposed-dimension, jointly trained contribution-routed split SAE with an aligned wrong-control suite.
gate.fail_action: Close the contribution-mode split family before trainable architecture development; do not run full7.
